scope: Bibliographic references, source versions and mathematical hypothesis adapters for the finite-cover computation.

conventions.e: all minimal generators, including those in [c,c+m)

sources.title: On numerical semigroups with at most 12 left elements
sources.hypotheses: Thm3.1: q>=4 and all A_i empty for 1<=i<ceil(q/2); no n bound. Thm4.1: n<=12. Prop2.7: universal W>=W0.
sources.application: Exact shifted layers, full P, and zero-inclusive L; W=W0+|P intersect[c,c+m)|(n-q).
sources.limits: Historical open>=13 sentence is dated2020. Negative W0 does not refute W.

sources.title: Families of Eliahou semigroups linked to Farey intervals
sources.hypotheses: All numerical semigroups with c<=200 inclusive.
sources.application: Bacher k=n, ell=left primitives,r=right primitives; full e=ell+r; W=k(ell+r)-c.
sources.limits: c<=320 assumes Conjecture2.5; c<=400 assumes further conjectures and the restriction ell<=7. Neither larger range is imported.

sources.title: A verification of Wilf's conjecture up to genus 100
sources.hypotheses: Every numerical semigroup with genus g<=100.
sources.application: Unrestricted g<=100; g=c-n so c<=n+100. Exact modern primary corroboration of classical e<=3.
sources.limits: The separate genus120 result requires m|c and is not imported.

sources.title: A graph-theoretic approach to Wilf's conjecture
sources.publication: Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 27(2) (2020), P2.15; DOI 10.37236/9106
sources.hypotheses: Theorem1.1 requires e>=m/3. Separate proof-level consequence: for every S, e>=4,q>=4,tau(X)<=2q-1 imply W>=0; no ratio hypothesis.
sources.application: tau(X)=n_left-q; paper n=|V| renamed b, graph delta renamed depth_G. Maximum matching counts touched vertices, loops once. Cor3.21 counts distinct weak-edge weights.
sources.limits: §5.8 LK5 is corrected to K5 by Prop5.7; §5.2 loopless star uses d<=b (actually b-1), with displayed final expression a conservative bound. Notation2.3 HTML rho typo corrected by c=qm-rho. Details in IMPORTS_v1.txt. No independently numbered small-tau theorem is invented.

sources.title: Wilf's conjecture and Macaulay's theorem
sources.publication: Journal of the European Mathematical Society 20(9) (2018), 2105–2129; DOI 10.4171/JEMS/807
sources.hypotheses: Standard graded commutative algebra over a field, degree d>=1. Use proper homogeneous quotient over Q and ordinary total degree. Numerical q=3 result; q=2 by Prop3.13; q=1 elementary.
sources.application: Hilbert growth h_(d+1)<=M_d(h_d); small positive arguments completed by Gao§1, zero endpoint directly by degree1 generation. Shifted A_i do not supply grading.
sources.limits: Shifted numerical Ai do not automatically form a standard grading. §7 true grading requires extra set-addition hypotheses. Classical growth and its small extremal values receive prior credit.

sources.title: On numerical semigroups
sources.hypotheses: Every numerical semigroup with full embedding dimension e<=3.
sources.limits: Publisher dates volume35 pp63–83/issue December1986; revised and accepted2January1987; EMA bibliography1987, Bacher bibliography1986. DOI fixed; bibliographic year conventions differ between sources. No original theorem locator invented.

sources.title: Oracle-Tree Forcing and Wilfs Inequality for Thirteen Left Elements
sources.hypotheses: The thirteen-left-element result is cited as the predecessor of the present finite cover.
sources.application: Predecessor credit; not a dispatch leaf in the finite cover for 14..37.
sources.limits: The predecessor is not an input to the finite computation for 14..37.

sources.title: Some results related to Macaulay's Theorem about Hilbert functions and applications
sources.hypotheses: Every positive a and positive degree d have truncated binomial expansion; §1 quotient theorem is over characteristic-zero field.
sources.application: All small positive Macaulay values available; M_d(0)=0 supplied by elementary algebra. Q meets characteristic-zero setup; algebraic closure in abstract not used.
sources.limits: Printed d>=0 in Thm1.1 is not imported at d=0: source representation is for positive degree. No Hermitian/sum-of-squares claim or historical priority assertion imported.
